decisions.rationale: The extract states that the album begins with a teacher calling roll, reaching Hill’s name several times with no answer, then moving on to teach. It also states that Ras Baraka, described as a poet, eighth-grade teacher, and later Newark mayor, led the lesson.

The extract attributed to Nobles says that “Forgive Them Father” and “Lost Ones” were made at the Bob Marley Museum on 56 Hope Road. It also says that is why Hill says, “I was hopeless, now I’m on Hope Road.”

The Nobles extract states that a female group called Ex Factor was signed to Arista and that they did a song called “Ex Factor” for them. It then says “Loved Real Hard Once” was retitled “When It Hurts So Bad” and that those were the first two records they worked on.

The extract attributed to Che Vicious says he made “Zion” during one of his 20-minute sessions in a hot Brooklyn brownstone studio. It also says Hill teared up and said she had an idea for a song about her baby but did not know what the music should sound like until hearing that track.

The Nobles extract states that the title for “Doo Wop (That Thing)” came from a box set labeled “doo wop” on the floor. It also says Nobles added a heavy drum to give the music edge and something hip-hop.

The extract attributed to Commissioner Gordon says that when James Poyser came in for “Superstar,” they rented an old harpsichord that fell out of tune quickly. It states that they had to have the tuner there and that the instrument was out of tune after James finished playing it once.

The extract says that on “Final Hour” Hill breaks down why she is one of the finest wordsmiths of her generation. It includes the quoted thesis, topic, pieces, and introduce/produce lines from the claim.
The Nobles extract states that they started working on a song called “Loved Real Hard Once.” It directly says the title was switched to “When It Hurts So Bad.”

The Nobles extract says they were discussing Hill’s relationship in the little studio in her attic in South Orange and that this is how “I Used to Love Him” came about. It also states, “It was about ‘Clef.”

The extract attributed to Nobles states that “Forgive Them Father” and “Lost Ones” were made at the Bob Marley Museum on 56 Hope Road. That directly supports the claim about where “Forgive Them Father” was made.

The extract states that Hill’s “Jack ya, jack ya, jack ya body” line in “Every Ghetto, Every City” references “Jack Your Body.” It identifies that song as a 1986 club anthem by Chicago DJ/producer Steve ‘Silk’ Hurley.
The D’Angelo extract says that when he and Lauryn went into the studio together, he laid down his vocals in the course of an hour. This directly matches the claim.
The John Legend extract says Hill was working on “Everything Is Everything” and asked him to play piano on the track. It also says he was playing along with a string part that was already there.
The extract says that on the title track Hill reaches the apogee of the cycle by learning love of self. This directly supports the quoted characterization in the claim.
The Commissioner Gordon extract states that “Can’t Take My Eyes Off of You” was never meant to be a commercial single. It also says it was originally recorded for the Conspiracy Theory soundtrack.
The extract identifies Candice Anderson as a backup singer and says “Tell Him” took a while. It gives the reason that Hill is very particular about how she wants it to sound.
